chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who had a debt owed to him by another man, and the debtor died leaving two executors (wasiyyan). Is it permissible to pay one of the two executors without the other? He said: 'It is not correct unless the ruler has divided the wealth between them, placing half in the hand of this one and half in the hand of the other, or if they both meet by the command of the ruler.'
ai.seo_question: How should a debt be paid if the deceased left two executors?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural safeguards in Shia jurisprudence for debt repayment when multiple executors are involved, emphasizing the necessity of judicial oversight (*hukm al-sultan*) to prevent unilateral appropriation of funds. Imam al-Rida (AS) stipulates that payment to a single executor is invalid unless the estate has been formally partitioned by authority or both executors are jointly present, thereby ensuring transparency and protecting the rights of the creditor and the other heir.
